From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA redlines: follow-the-sun support & maintenance windows

Team —

I reviewed Cerulean's annotated PDF. High-level positions/legal redlines I'd like to propose before we send back:

1) Credit cap: propose a monthly credit cap equal to 10% of monthly recurring charges (MRC). Larger caps (20%+) materially alter economics and need exec approval.

2) Scheduled maintenance: exclude from uptime only if Redwood provides >=72 hours' notice and the maintenance occurs within mutually agreed maintenance windows (we should define weekly slots by region).

3) Evidence and dispute resolution: require Redwood's operational metrics + customer-facing uptime report; disputes escalate to a 10-business-day review with automated snapshot logs as evidence.

4) Response time SLOs: we can accept a 15-minute P1 (SEV1) target for production-impact incidents in the follow-the-sun model, with an operational runbook and on-call roster documented as an appendix to the Order Form.

5) Blackout windows & product launches: propose a carve-out for customer-declared launch blackout days (limited to 3 per year) where both parties align 30 days in advance. Any additional blackout days should be handled case-by-case.

I'll convert these into track-changes on the MSA/Order Form and send back with inline comments. If the customer pushes on the cap we can escalate to Finance/Sales leadership.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: Legal_markup_MSA_Cerulean_v1.pdf (track changes)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Apr 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Ops notes: on-call, SLO ladder & maintenance windows

Folks — ops perspective below, pulled from our Dedicated/Private playbook and tailored for Cerulean's follow-the-sun ask: 

- Proposed SLOs (by incident severity):
  • P1 (Service down / critical user impact): response ack in 15 minutes, remediation timeline TBD per incident.
  • P2 (Partial degradation): response ack in 1 hour.
  • P3 (Minor): response ack in 4 hours.

- Regional follow-the-sun handoffs: 1-hour overlap between APAC->EU and EU->US shifts to ensure context transfer.

- Maintenance windows: we recommend a regional weekly 2-hour window (customer selectable slot) + a monthly global 4-hour maintenance for infra upgrades. All scheduled windows require 72 hours' notice.

- Evidence: automated uptime snapshots (per-az) and request logs will be provided; we can include a weekly uptime digest in the Console for the customer.

- Canary rollout suggestion: 48-hour canary on 10% traffic, monitor latency/availability, then region-by-region 72-hour ramp with immediate rollback on >1% error delta.

Attaching a short ops runbook stub. Will sync with Laura on where to reference the runbook in the Order Form appendix.

- Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Production Operations, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Consolidated proposal: Order Form SLO table + rollout plan (attached)

Sean — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear table. A few points from our side after internal review:

1) Credit cap: 10% still seems low for our risk profile; would Redwood consider 15–20% MRC as a compromise? Our procurement lead is pushing for 20%.
2) P1 response: can we consider 1 hour instead of 15 minutes for our non-US regions given current SLAs with our platform team? We can accept the 15-minute target for US-based critical incidents if you can make that regionally explicit in the Order Form.
3) Maintenance: the 72-hour notice is fine; we ask for a simple blackout exception calendar for our quarterly launches (we have 2–3 per year).

If we can get alignment on a 15% cap + regional P1 carve-outs, we can sign once Laura's final markup is in DocuSign. Please let me know if Redwood needs any exec sign-off for the cap change; we can route pricing accordingly.

Thanks —
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Infrastructure, Cerulean AI
